title: Insecure Mixing of Secrets and Structure in Configuration Files
damaged_code:
```yaml
# 5000-line XML/YAML dependency injection configuration
app_structure:
  service_a:
    class: "com.acme.ServiceA"
    database:
      driver: "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"
      # DB Password mixed with dependency injection plumbing
      password: "SuperSecretProdDBPassword123!"
```
pattern: Placing production database passwords, API keys, or security credentials inside monolithic dependency injection or application wiring files.
why_bad: Forces operators to modify massive structural configurations just to perform a key rotation. Editing a 5000-line configuration creates substantial risk of introducing typos, causing outages, or accidentally leaking credentials via shared plumbing files.
detection: The presence of plaintext password literals or security keys inside large framework orchestration configurations (such as Spring XML, Kubernetes manifests, YAML files).
counterexample:
```yaml
app_structure:
  service_a:
    class: "com.acme.ServiceA"
    database:
      driver: "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver"
      password_env_var: "DATABASE_PASSWORD"
```
fix: Isolate production passwords into separate, restricted configuration files owned strictly by the application owner, or inject secrets directly via environment variables.
source: `Michael T. Nygard - Release It! (2007)`, Ch 12, p. 272-273.
